title: Missing-Signal Detector by Morning
dataSources: Daily life scores (`lifescore:daily`), personal SLO status (`personalslo:status`), cross-signal correlations (`correlation:pair`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The meta layer — correlating every `index=personal` feed (sleep, activity, mood, weather, spend, productivity, home telemetry) into daily life scores, personal SLOs, and cross-signal anomaly detection, all computed in Splunk.
spl:
index=personal earliest=-24h
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen by sourcetype
| eval age_hours=round((now()-last_seen)/3600,1)
| where age_hours>24
| sort - age_hours
description: Shows which feeds failed to report in the last day and may have fallen out of your personal data picture.
value: A digital twin is only as useful as its freshest signals, so silence is a first-class problem.
implementation: Review all `index=personal` feeds daily; alert when a sourcetype has gone stale beyond one day.
visualization: Table of sourcetypes with hours since last event.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks which parts of your personal data picture have gone silent, so the whole dashboard does not quietly rot from missing pieces.
